subject: UniProtKB:P54745
description: MngA is one 658-residue EIIABC chain. MC4100 mngA deletion loses MG transport and pACS31 restores it; inverted membranes plus general PTS extracts and PEP form MG-P. This is not a purified three-protein reconstitution. Separate intact-cell uptake comparisons in MG-induced MC4100 reported weak reduction with glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect with trehalose, and no observed reduction with fructose, maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol. The Discussion instead describes mannose and those three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar radiolabeled MG; the mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension remains unresolved. These are uptake comparisons, not direct binding, a proven competitive mechanism or inhibition constants. Separately, 300 mM NaCl during growth did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%; this is an induction endpoint, distinct from the KM522 500 mM salt-protection experiment and from a direct catalytic salt effect. None of these whole-cell comparisons is attributed to the pACS31 inverted-membrane assay.
